import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Performs a standard 2D convolution operation with a square input and square kernel.

    Args:
        in_channels (int): Number of channels in the input tensor.
        out_channels (int): Number of channels produced by the convolution.
        kernel_size (int): Size of the square convolution kernel.
        stride (int, optional): Stride of the convolution. Defaults to 1.
        padding (int, optional): Padding applied to the input. Defaults to 0.
        dilation (int, optional): Spacing between kernel elements. Defaults to 1.
        groups (int, optional): Number of blocked connections from input channels to output channels. Defaults to 1.
        bias (bool, optional): If `True`, adds a learnable bias to the output. Defaults to `False`.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels: int, out_channels: int, kernel_size: int, stride: int = 1, padding: int = 0, dilation: int = 1, groups: int = 1, bias: bool = False):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.conv2d = nn.Conv2d(in_channels, out_channels, (kernel_size, kernel_size), stride=stride, padding=padding, dilation=dilation, groups=groups, bias=bias)
        
    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        """
        Performs the 2D convolution.

        Args:
            x (torch.Tensor): Input tensor of shape (batch_size, in_channels, height, width).

        Returns:
            torch.Tensor: Output tensor of shape (batch_size, out_channels, height_out, width_out).
        """
        return self.conv2d(x)

A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.transpose
transpose is written `%r = "stablehlo.transpose"(%x) {permutation = array<i64: 1, 0>} : (tensor<2x3xf32>) -> tensor<3x2xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.transpose"(%x) {permutation = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. permutation must be a permutation of the numbers 0 to rank minus one. Result dimension d has the size of operand dimension permutation[d].     def __init__(self, in_features, out_features):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.gemm = nn.Linear(in_features, out_features)

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.convolution"(%lhs, %rhs) {window_strides = array<i64: ...>, padding = dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<(N-2)x2xi64>, lhs_dilation = array<i64: ...>, rhs_dilation = array<i64: ...>, dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.conv<[...]x[...]->[...]>, feature_group_count = G : i64, batch_group_count = 1 : i64} : (T_lhs, T_rhs) -> T_out`. The input, kernel and result have the same element type. dimension_numbers lists the role of each dimension: in the input and output b is batch, f is feature and 0, 1, ... are spatial dimensions; in the kernel o is output feature, i is input feature and 0, 1, ... are spatial; for example `[b, f, 0, 1]x[o, i, 0, 1]->[b, f, 0, 1]` is the NCHW / OIHW layout. window_strides, lhs_dilation and rhs_dilation each have one positive entry per spatial dimension, and padding has one [low, high] pair per spatial dimension. ### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). dot_general is written `%r = "stablehlo.dot_general"(%a, %b) {dot_dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.dot<lhs_batching_dimensions = [0], rhs_batching_dimensions = [0], lhs_contracting_dimensions = [2], rhs_contracting_dimensions = [1]>} : (tensor<2x3x4xf32>, tensor<2x4x5xf32>) -> tensor<2x3x5xf32>`, and the batching fields may be omitted when there are no batch dimensions. ### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.reduce
reduce is written with a body region, for example `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<f32>, %b: tensor<f32>): %s = "stablehlo.add"(%a, %b) : (tensor<f32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<f32> "stablehlo.return"(%s) : (tensor<f32>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<4x3xf32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<4xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<E>, %b: tensor<E>): ... "stablehlo.return"(%v) : (tensor<E>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in, tensor<E>) -> T_out`. The init value is a rank-0 tensor whose element type equals the input's, and the body takes two rank-0 tensors of that element type and returns one. The result shape is the input shape with the reduced dimensions removed, not kept as size-1 dimensions. The reduced dimensions must be distinct and each between 0 and the input rank minus one. The init value may be combined an implementation-defined number of times, so it must be the identity of the body: zero for add, negative infinity for maximum and positive infinity for minimum. reduce can reduce several inputs at once: with N inputs and N init values the body takes 2N rank-0 arguments (the N accumulators, then the N elements) and returns N values, which is how an argmax carries a value together with its index. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types.

In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. 
### stablehlo.reduce
reduce is written with a body region, for example `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<f32>, %b: tensor<f32>): %s = "stablehlo.add"(%a, %b) : (tensor<f32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<f32> "stablehlo.return"(%s) : (tensor<f32>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<4x3xf32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<4xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<E>, %b: tensor<E>): ... "stablehlo.return"(%v) : (tensor<E>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in, tensor<E>) -> T_out`. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. Reference documentation:

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. 
### stablehlo.reduce
reduce is written with a body region, for example `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<f32>, %b: tensor<f32>): %s = "stablehlo.add"(%a, %b) : (tensor<f32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<f32> "stablehlo.return"(%s) : (tensor<f32>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<4x3xf32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<4xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<E>, %b: tensor<E>): ... "stablehlo.return"(%v) : (tensor<E>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in, tensor<E>) -> T_out`. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`.

A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires.

The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`.

All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. "stablehlo.return"(%v) : (tensor<E>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in, tensor<E>) -> T_out`. ### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`. 
### Element-wise operations

In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types.

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.clamp
clamp takes its operands in the order min, operand, max: `%r = "stablehlo.clamp"(%lo, %x, %hi) : (tensor<f32>, tensor<4xf32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<4xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.clamp"(%min, %operand, %max) : (T_min, T, T_max) -> T`. min, operand and max share one element type, and the result has the operand's type. min and max are each either rank 0 or the same shape as the operand. Each result element is the operand element raised to at least min and then lowered to at most max. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`.

Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types. 
### stablehlo.math
Further element-wise math operations are written like `%r = stablehlo.tanh %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise log, log_plus_one, exponential_minus_one, logistic, floor, sign) and `%r = stablehlo.power %a, %b : tensor<4xf32>`. ### stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim
broadcast_in_dim is written `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<2x3xf32>`. The result has the same element type as the operand. broadcast_dimensions must contain exactly one entry for each dimension of the operand. ### stablehlo.reshape
reshape is written `%r = stablehlo.reshape %x : (tensor<2x3xf32>) -> tensor<6xf32>`. In general form: `%r = stablehlo.reshape %x : (T_in) -> T_out`. The operand and the result must contain the same number of elements. reshape keeps elements in row-major (lexicographic) order and never reorders them, so changing the order of axes requires a transpose.

In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.convolution"(%lhs, %rhs) {window_strides = array<i64: ...>, padding = dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<(N-2)x2xi64>, lhs_dilation = array<i64: ...>, rhs_dilation = array<i64: ...>, dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.conv<[...]x[...]->[...]>, feature_group_count = G : i64, batch_group_count = 1 : i64} : (T_lhs, T_rhs) -> T_out`. compare is written `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction LT>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type FLOAT>} : (tensor<4xf32>, tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xi1>`. ### stablehlo.select
select is written `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %on_true, %on_false) : (tensor<2x2xi1>, tensor<2x2xf32>, tensor<2x2xf32>) -> tensor<2x2xf32>`. ### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Simple model that performs RMS Normalization.
    """
    def __init__(self, num_features: int, eps: float = 1e-5):
        """
        Initializes the RMSNorm layer.

        Args:
            num_features (int): Number of features in the input tensor.
            eps (float, optional): A small value added to the denominator to avoid division by zero. Defaults to 1e-5.
        """
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.num_features = num_features
        self.eps = eps

        Returns:
            torch.Tensor: Output tensor with RMS Normalization applied, same shape as input.

        # Calculate the RMS along the feature dimension
        rms = torch.sqrt(torch.mean(x ** 2, dim=1, keepdim=True) + self.eps)

    """
    def __init__(self, num_features: int, eps: float = 1e-5):
        """
        Initializes the RMSNorm layer.

        Args:
            num_features (int): Number of features in the input tensor.
            eps (float, optional): A small value added to the denominator to avoid division by zero. Defaults to 1e-5.
        """
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.num_features = num_features
        self.eps = eps

A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`.

A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. 
### stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim
broadcast_in_dim is written `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<2x3xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. 
### stablehlo.convert
convert is written `%r = stablehlo.convert %x : (tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xi32>`. In general form: `%r = stablehlo.convert %x : (T_in) -> T_out`.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Model that performs average pooling, 3D transposed convolution, clamping,
    spatial softmax, and multiplication by a learnable scale.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, stride, padding, output_padding, pool_kernel_size, clamp_min, clamp_max):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.avg_pool = nn.AvgPool3d(pool_kernel_size)
        self.conv_transpose = nn.ConvTranspose3d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, stride=stride, padding=padding, output_padding=output_padding)
        self.clamp_min = clamp_min
        self.clamp_max = clamp_max
        self.scale = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(1, out_channels, 1, 1, 1))

    def forward(self, x):
        """
        Args:
            x (torch.Tensor): Input tensor of shape (batch_size, in_channels, depth, height, width).

        Returns:
            torch.Tensor: Output tensor of shape (batch_size, out_channels, depth, height, width).
        """
        x = self.avg_pool(x)
        x = self.conv_transpose(x)
        x = torch.clamp(x, self.clamp_min, self.clamp_max)
        b, c, d, h, w = x.shape
        x = x.view(b, c, -1)                     # flatten spatial dims
        x = torch.softmax(x, dim=2)
        x = x.view(b, c, d, h, w)
        x = x * self.scale
        return x

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.dot_general
dot_general is written `%r = "stablehlo.dot_general"(%a, %b) {dot_dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.dot<lhs_batching_dimensions = [0], rhs_batching_dimensions = [0], lhs_contracting_dimensions = [2], rhs_contracting_dimensions = [1]>} : (tensor<2x3x4xf32>, tensor<2x4x5xf32>) -> tensor<2x3x5xf32>`, and the batching fields may be omitted when there are no batch dimensions. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.dot_general"(%a, %b) {dot_dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.dot<lhs_batching_dimensions = [...], rhs_batching_dimensions = [...], lhs_contracting_dimensions = [...], rhs_contracting_dimensions = [...]>} : (T_a, T_b) -> T_r`; empty batching fields optional. lhs and rhs must have the same element type. The result dimensions are, in order, the batch dimensions, then the remaining lhs dimensions in their original order, then the remaining rhs dimensions in their original order. Each paired batch dimension and each paired contracting dimension must have equal sizes on the lhs and the rhs. The lhs and rhs must list the same number of batch dimensions and the same number of contracting dimensions, and no dimension may be both a batch and a contracting dimension. Each result element is the sum, over all contracting indices, of products of lhs and rhs elements at the same batch index; there is no implicit transpose, so the choice of contracting dimensions decides which axes are summed.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Model that performs average pooling, 3D transposed convolution, clamping,
    spatial softmax, and multiplication by a learnable scale.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, stride, padding, output_padding, pool_kernel_size, clamp_min, clamp_max):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.avg_pool = nn.AvgPool3d(pool_kernel_size)
        self.conv_transpose = nn.ConvTranspose3d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, stride=stride, padding=padding, output_padding=output_padding)
        self.clamp_min = clamp_min
        self.clamp_max = clamp_max
        self.scale = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(1, out_channels, 1, 1, 1))

    def forward(self, x):
        """
        Args:
            x (torch.Tensor): Input tensor of shape (batch_size, in_channels, depth, height, width).

        Returns:
            torch.Tensor: Output tensor of shape (batch_size, out_channels, depth, height, width).
        """
        x = self.avg_pool(x)
        x = self.conv_transpose(x)
        x = torch.clamp(x, self.clamp_min, self.clamp_max)
        b, c, d, h, w = x.shape
        x = x.view(b, c, -1)                     # flatten spatial dims
        x = torch.softmax(x, dim=2)
        x = x.view(b, c, d, h, w)
        x = x * self.scale
        return x

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. 
### stablehlo.dot_general
dot_general is written `%r = "stablehlo.dot_general"(%a, %b) {dot_dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.dot<lhs_batching_dimensions = [0], rhs_batching_dimensions = [0], lhs_contracting_dimensions = [2], rhs_contracting_dimensions = [1]>} : (tensor<2x3x4xf32>, tensor<2x4x5xf32>) -> tensor<2x3x5xf32>`, and the batching fields may be omitted when there are no batch dimensions. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.dot_general"(%a, %b) {dot_dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.dot<lhs_batching_dimensions = [...], rhs_batching_dimensions = [...], lhs_contracting_dimensions = [...], rhs_contracting_dimensions = [...]>} : (T_a, T_b) -> T_r`; empty batching fields optional.

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.dot_general
dot_general is written `%r = "stablehlo.dot_general"(%a, %b) {dot_dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.dot<lhs_batching_dimensions = [0], rhs_batching_dimensions = [0], lhs_contracting_dimensions = [2], rhs_contracting_dimensions = [1]>} : (tensor<2x3x4xf32>, tensor<2x4x5xf32>) -> tensor<2x3x5xf32>`, and the batching fields may be omitted when there are no batch dimensions. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.dot_general"(%a, %b) {dot_dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.dot<lhs_batching_dimensions = [...], rhs_batching_dimensions = [...], lhs_contracting_dimensions = [...], rhs_contracting_dimensions = [...]>} : (T_a, T_b) -> T_r`; empty batching fields optional. lhs and rhs must have the same element type. The result dimensions are, in order, the batch dimensions, then the remaining lhs dimensions in their original order, then the remaining rhs dimensions in their original order. Each paired batch dimension and each paired contracting dimension must have equal sizes on the lhs and the rhs. The lhs and rhs must list the same number of batch dimensions and the same number of contracting dimensions, and no dimension may be both a batch and a contracting dimension. Each result element is the sum, over all contracting indices, of products of lhs and rhs elements at the same batch index; there is no implicit transpose, so the choice of contracting dimensions decides which axes are summed.

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`.

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.reduce
reduce is written with a body region, for example `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<f32>, %b: tensor<f32>): %s = "stablehlo.add"(%a, %b) : (tensor<f32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<f32> "stablehlo.return"(%s) : (tensor<f32>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<4x3xf32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<4xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<E>, %b: tensor<E>): ... "stablehlo.return"(%v) : (tensor<E>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in, tensor<E>) -> T_out`. The init value is a rank-0 tensor whose element type equals the input's, and the body takes two rank-0 tensors of that element type and returns one. The result shape is the input shape with the reduced dimensions removed, not kept as size-1 dimensions. The reduced dimensions must be distinct and each between 0 and the input rank minus one. The init value may be combined an implementation-defined number of times, so it must be the identity of the body: zero for add, negative infinity for maximum and positive infinity for minimum. reduce can reduce several inputs at once: with N inputs and N init values the body takes 2N rank-0 arguments (the N accumulators, then the N elements) and returns N values, which is how an argmax carries a value together with its index. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types.

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.dynamic_slice
dynamic_slice takes the operand followed by one rank-0 integer start index per dimension: `%r = "stablehlo.dynamic_slice"(%x, %i, %j) {slice_sizes = array<i64: 2, 4>} : (tensor<8x4xf32>, tensor<i32>, tensor<i32>) -> tensor<2x4xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.dynamic_slice"(%x, %s0, ..., %s_{R-1}) {slice_sizes = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in, tensor<I>, ...) -> T_out`. All start indices are rank-0 tensors of the same integer type, and the result element type equals the operand's. There is one start index and one slice size per operand dimension, each slice size is at most the dimension size, and the result shape equals slice_sizes. Before slicing, each start index is clamped into the range 0 to dimension size minus slice size, so an out-of-range start never fails but shifts the window inside the tensor. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`.

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.concatenate
concatenate is written `%r = "stablehlo.concatenate"(%a, %b) {dimension = 0 : i64} : (tensor<3x2xf32>, tensor<1x2xf32>) -> tensor<4x2xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.concatenate"(%a, %b, ...) {dimension = d : i64} : (T_a, T_b, ...) -> T_out`. All inputs and the result have the same element type. All inputs must have the same shape except along the concatenation dimension, which must be between 0 and the rank minus one. Along the concatenation dimension the result size is the sum of the input sizes. Inputs are placed one after another along the dimension in argument order.

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types. 
### stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim
broadcast_in_dim is written `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<2x3xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. The result has the same element type as the operand. broadcast_dimensions must contain exactly one entry for each dimension of the operand. Each entry of broadcast_dimensions is a distinct result dimension index between 0 and the result rank minus one. Operand dimension d must either have size 1 or have the same size as result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d]. Operand dimension d is placed at result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d] and the data is copied along every other result dimension, while an operand dimension of size 1 is repeated across its whole result dimension. 
### stablehlo.reshape
reshape is written `%r = stablehlo.reshape %x : (tensor<2x3xf32>) -> tensor<6xf32>`. In general form: `%r = stablehlo.reshape %x : (T_in) -> T_out`. The operand and the result must contain the same number of elements. reshape keeps elements in row-major (lexicographic) order and never reorders them, so changing the order of axes requires a transpose. 
### stablehlo.convolution

In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.convolution"(%lhs, %rhs) {window_strides = array<i64: ...>, padding = dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<(N-2)x2xi64>, lhs_dilation = array<i64: ...>, rhs_dilation = array<i64: ...>, dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.conv<[...]x[...]->[...]>, feature_group_count = G : i64, batch_group_count = 1 : i64} : (T_lhs, T_rhs) -> T_out`. The input, kernel and result have the same element type. dimension_numbers lists the role of each dimension: in the input and output b is batch, f is feature and 0, 1, ... are spatial dimensions; in the kernel o is output feature, i is input feature and 0, 1, ... are spatial; for example `[b, f, 0, 1]x[o, i, 0, 1]->[b, f, 0, 1]` is the NCHW / OIHW layout. window_strides, lhs_dilation and rhs_dilation each have one positive entry per spatial dimension, and padding has one [low, high] pair per spatial dimension. Each output spatial size is floor((low + (n - 1) * lhs_dilation + 1 + high - ((k - 1) * rhs_dilation + 1)) / stride) + 1, where n is the input size and k the kernel size along that dimension. The kernel's input-feature size equals the input feature size divided by feature_group_count, and the kernel's output-feature size, which becomes the output feature size, must be divisible by feature_group_count. convolution computes a cross-correlation without flipping the kernel; rhs_dilation spaces out kernel taps (dilated convolution), lhs_dilation inserts lhs_dilation - 1 zeros between input elements (used for transposed convolution together with a spatially reversed kernel), and feature_group_count splits the features into independent groups (grouped or depthwise convolution). 
### stablehlo.reduce
reduce is written with a body region, for example `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<f32>, %b: tensor<f32>): %s = "stablehlo.add"(%a, %b) : (tensor<f32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<f32> "stablehlo.return"(%s) : (tensor<f32>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<4x3xf32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<4xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<E>, %b: tensor<E>): ... "stablehlo.return"(%v) : (tensor<E>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in, tensor<E>) -> T_out`. The init value is a rank-0 tensor whose element type equals the input's, and the body takes two rank-0 tensors of that element type and returns one. The result shape is the input shape with the reduced dimensions removed, not kept as size-1 dimensions. The reduced dimensions must be distinct and each between 0 and the input rank minus one. The init value may be combined an implementation-defined number of times, so it must be the identity of the body: zero for add, negative infinity for maximum and positive infinity for minimum. reduce can reduce several inputs at once: with N inputs and N init values the body takes 2N rank-0 arguments (the N accumulators, then the N elements) and returns N values, which is how an argmax carries a value together with its index. 
### stablehlo.reduce_window
reduce_window is written with a body region, for example `%r = "stablehlo.reduce_window"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<f32>, %b: tensor<f32>): %m = stablehlo.maximum %a, %b : tensor<f32> stablehlo.return %m : tensor<f32> }) {window_dimensions = array<i64: 1, 1, 2, 2>, window_strides = array<i64: 1, 1, 2, 2>, padding = dense<0> : tensor<4x2xi64>} : (tensor<2x3x8x8xf32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<2x3x4x4xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.reduce_window"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<E>, %b: tensor<E>): ... stablehlo.return %v : tensor<E> }) {window_dimensions = array<i64: ...>, window_strides = array<i64: ...>, base_dilations = array<i64: ...>?, window_dilations = array<i64: ...>?, padding = dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>?} : (T_in, tensor<E>) -> T_out`. The init value is a rank-0 tensor of the input's element type, and the body takes and returns rank-0 tensors of that type. window_dimensions, window_strides, base_dilations and window_dilations each have one positive entry for every input dimension, including non-spatial ones, and padding has one [low, high] pair for every input dimension. Each output size is floor((low + (n - 1) * base_dilation + 1 + high - ((w - 1) * window_dilation + 1)) / stride) + 1, where n is the input size and w the window size along that dimension. Each output element reduces one window of the padded input with the body; padded positions hold the init value, so they participate in the reduction and an average must divide by the intended element count explicitly.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Model that performs a 3D convolution, applies Softmax, and performs two max pooling operations.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, pool_kernel_size):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.conv = nn.Conv3d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size)
        self.pool1 = nn.MaxPool3d(pool_kernel_size)
        self.pool2 = nn.MaxPool3d(pool_kernel_size)

    def forward(self, x):
        """
        Args:
            x: Input tensor of shape (batch_size, in_channels, depth, height, width)
        Returns:
            Output tensor of shape (batch_size, out_channels, depth', height', width') where depth', height', width' are the dimensions after pooling.
        """
        x = self.conv(x)
        x = torch.softmax(x, dim=1)
        x = self.pool1(x)
        x = self.pool2(x)
        return x

depth, height, width = 16, 7, 7
kernel_size = 3
pool_kernel_size = 2

def get_inputs():
    return [torch.rand(batch_size, in_channels, depth, height, width)]

def get_init_inputs():
    return [in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, pool_kernel_size]

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types. 
### stablehlo.math
Further element-wise math operations are written like `%r = stablehlo.tanh %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise log, log_plus_one, exponential_minus_one, logistic, floor, sign) and `%r = stablehlo.power %a, %b : tensor<4xf32>`. ### stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim
broadcast_in_dim is written `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<2x3xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. Operand dimension d must either have size 1 or have the same size as result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d]. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. ### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. ### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. ### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`. 
### stablehlo.logical
Logical operations on booleans are written `%r = stablehlo.and %a, %b : tensor<4xi1>` (likewise or) and `%r = stablehlo.not %a : tensor<4xi1>`. In general form: `%r = stablehlo.{and|or} %a, %b : tensor<...xi1>`; `%r = stablehlo.not %a : tensor<...xi1>`. and, or and not require operands of boolean or integer type with identical types, and act bitwise on integers. 
### stablehlo.reduce
reduce is written with a body region, for example `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<f32>, %b: tensor<f32>): %s = "stablehlo.add"(%a, %b) : (tensor<f32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<f32> "stablehlo.return"(%s) : (tensor<f32>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<4x3xf32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<4xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<E>, %b: tensor<E>): ... "stablehlo.return"(%v) : (tensor<E>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in, tensor<E>) -> T_out`. The init value is a rank-0 tensor whose element type equals the input's, and the body takes two rank-0 tensors of that element type and returns one. The result shape is the input shape with the reduced dimensions removed, not kept as size-1 dimensions. The reduced dimensions must be distinct and each between 0 and the input rank minus one. The init value may be combined an implementation-defined number of times, so it must be the identity of the body: zero for add, negative infinity for maximum and positive infinity for minimum. reduce can reduce several inputs at once: with N inputs and N init values the body takes 2N rank-0 arguments (the N accumulators, then the N elements) and returns N values, which is how an argmax carries a value together with its index. 
### stablehlo.compare
compare is written `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction LT>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type FLOAT>} : (tensor<4xf32>, tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xi1>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction DIR>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type CT>} : (T, T) -> tensor<...xi1>`. lhs and rhs have the same element type and the result element type is i1. compare_type is optional, but if given it must be FLOAT, TOTALORDER or WEAKORDER for floating-point operands and NOTYPE or SIGNED for signed integers. lhs, rhs and the result must have the same shape. The direction EQ, NE, GE, GT, LE or LT tests lhs against rhs element-wise, for example GT gives true where lhs > rhs. 
### stablehlo.select
select is written `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %on_true, %on_false) : (tensor<2x2xi1>, tensor<2x2xf32>, tensor<2x2xf32>) -> tensor<2x2xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %t, %f) : (tensor<...xi1>, T, T) -> T`. on_true, on_false and the result must have the same type. The predicate has element type i1 and is either rank 0 or the same shape as on_true. Each result element is taken from on_true where the predicate is true and from on_false otherwise. 
### stablehlo.iota
iota is written `%r = "stablehlo.iota"() {iota_dimension = 0 : i64} : () -> tensor<4x5xi32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.iota"() {iota_dimension = d : i64} : () -> T`. iota_dimension must be between 0 and the result rank minus one. Each output element equals its own index along iota_dimension, so values count 0, 1, 2, ... along that dimension and are constant along every other dimension; float element types are allowed.

Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. ### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once.
