### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. 
### stablehlo.transpose
transpose is written `%r = "stablehlo.transpose"(%x) {permutation = array<i64: 1, 0>} : (tensor<2x3xf32>) -> tensor<3x2xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.transpose"(%x) {permutation = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`.

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.transpose
transpose is written `%r = "stablehlo.transpose"(%x) {permutation = array<i64: 1, 0>} : (tensor<2x3xf32>) -> tensor<3x2xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.transpose"(%x) {permutation = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. permutation must be a permutation of the numbers 0 to rank minus one. Result dimension d has the size of operand dimension permutation[d]. Result dimension d is operand dimension permutation[d], so the element at result index i comes from the operand index whose dimension permutation[d] equals i[d].

    """

    """
    def __init__(self, in_features, out_features, bias=True):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.linear = nn.Linear(in_features, out_features, bias=bias)

        # LogSumExp

        # LeakyReLU

        # GELU

        x = torch.nn.functional.gelu(x)
        return x

Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types.

In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. The result has the same element type as the operand. broadcast_dimensions must contain exactly one entry for each dimension of the operand. Each entry of broadcast_dimensions is a distinct result dimension index between 0 and the result rank minus one. Operand dimension d must either have size 1 or have the same size as result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d]. Operand dimension d is placed at result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d] and the data is copied along every other result dimension, while an operand dimension of size 1 is repeated across its whole result dimension.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Model that performs a transposed convolution, applies Mish activation, adds a value, 
    applies Hardtanh activation, and scales the output.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, stride, padding, output_padding, add_value, scale):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.conv_transpose = nn.ConvTranspose2d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, stride, padding, output_padding)
        self.add_value = add_value
        self.scale = scale

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.conv_transpose(x)
        x = torch.nn.functional.mish(x) # Mish activation
        x = x + self.add_value
        x = torch.nn.functional.hardtanh(x, min_val=-1, max_val=1) # Hardtanh activation
        x = x * self.scale # Scaling
        return x

A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Model that performs a transposed convolution, applies Mish activation, adds a value, 
    applies Hardtanh activation, and scales the output.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, stride, padding, output_padding, add_value, scale):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.conv_transpose = nn.ConvTranspose2d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, stride, padding, output_padding)
        self.add_value = add_value
        self.scale = scale

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.conv_transpose(x)
        x = torch.nn.functional.mish(x) # Mish activation
        x = x + self.add_value
        x = torch.nn.functional.hardtanh(x, min_val=-1, max_val=1) # Hardtanh activation
        x = x * self.scale # Scaling
        return x

### Program structure and types

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim
broadcast_in_dim is written `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<2x3xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. The result has the same element type as the operand. broadcast_dimensions must contain exactly one entry for each dimension of the operand. Each entry of broadcast_dimensions is a distinct result dimension index between 0 and the result rank minus one. Operand dimension d must either have size 1 or have the same size as result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d]. Operand dimension d is placed at result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d] and the data is copied along every other result dimension, while an operand dimension of size 1 is repeated across its whole result dimension. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. import torch

class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Model that performs a transposed convolution, adds a bias term, clamps, scales, clamps, and divides.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, stride, padding, output_padding, bias_shape, scaling_factor):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.conv_transpose = nn.ConvTranspose2d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, stride=stride, padding=padding, output_padding=output_padding)
        self.bias = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(bias_shape)) 
        self.scaling_factor = scaling_factor

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.conv_transpose(x)
        x = x + self.bias
        x = torch.clamp(x, min=0.0, max=1.0)
        x = x * self.scaling_factor
        x = torch.clamp(x, min=0.0, max=1.0)
        x = x / self.scaling_factor
        return x

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types.

broadcast_in_dim is written `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<2x3xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. The result has the same element type as the operand. broadcast_dimensions must contain exactly one entry for each dimension of the operand. Each entry of broadcast_dimensions is a distinct result dimension index between 0 and the result rank minus one. Operand dimension d must either have size 1 or have the same size as result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d]. Operand dimension d is placed at result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d] and the data is copied along every other result dimension, while an operand dimension of size 1 is repeated across its whole result dimension.

reshape is written `%r = stablehlo.reshape %x : (tensor<2x3xf32>) -> tensor<6xf32>`. In general form: `%r = stablehlo.reshape %x : (T_in) -> T_out`. The operand and the result must contain the same number of elements. reshape keeps elements in row-major (lexicographic) order and never reorders them, so changing the order of axes requires a transpose.

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. ### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.iota
iota is written `%r = "stablehlo.iota"() {iota_dimension = 0 : i64} : () -> tensor<4x5xi32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.iota"() {iota_dimension = d : i64} : () -> T`. iota_dimension must be between 0 and the result rank minus one. Each output element equals its own index along iota_dimension, so values count 0, 1, 2, ... along that dimension and are constant along every other dimension; float element types are allowed. 
### stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim
broadcast_in_dim is written `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<2x3xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. The result has the same element type as the operand. broadcast_dimensions must contain exactly one entry for each dimension of the operand. Each entry of broadcast_dimensions is a distinct result dimension index between 0 and the result rank minus one. Operand dimension d must either have size 1 or have the same size as result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d]. Operand dimension d is placed at result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d] and the data is copied along every other result dimension, while an operand dimension of size 1 is repeated across its whole result dimension. 
### stablehlo.compare
compare is written `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction LT>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type FLOAT>} : (tensor<4xf32>, tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xi1>`. ### stablehlo.select
select is written `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %on_true, %on_false) : (tensor<2x2xi1>, tensor<2x2xf32>, tensor<2x2xf32>) -> tensor<2x2xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %t, %f) : (tensor<...xi1>, T, T) -> T`. on_true, on_false and the result must have the same type. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types. 
### stablehlo.math
Further element-wise math operations are written like `%r = stablehlo.tanh %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise log, log_plus_one, exponential_minus_one, logistic, floor, sign) and `%r = stablehlo.power %a, %b : tensor<4xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. ### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires.

class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Model that performs a transposed convolution, adds a value, takes the minimum, applies GELU, and multiplies by a value.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, stride, add_value, multiply_value):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.conv_transpose = nn.ConvTranspose2d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, stride=stride)
        self.add_value = add_value
        self.multiply_value = multiply_value

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.conv_transpose(x)
        x = x + self.add_value
        x = torch.min(x, torch.tensor(0.0, device=x.device))
        x = torch.nn.functional.gelu(x)
        x = x * self.multiply_value
        return x

class Model(nn.Module):

    def __init__(self, in_features, out_features, scaling_factor):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.matmul = nn.Linear(in_features, out_features)

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. 
### stablehlo.reduce
reduce is written with a body region, for example `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<f32>, %b: tensor<f32>): %s = "stablehlo.add"(%a, %b) : (tensor<f32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<f32> "stablehlo.return"(%s) : (tensor<f32>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<4x3xf32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<4xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<E>, %b: tensor<E>): ... "stablehlo.return"(%v) : (tensor<E>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in, tensor<E>) -> T_out`. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs).     """
    def __init__(self, in_features, out_features, scaling_factor):
        super(Model, self).__init__()

        original_x = x.clone().detach()
        x = x * self.scaling_factor
        x = x + original_x
        return x

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. 
### stablehlo.reverse
reverse is written `%r = "stablehlo.reverse"(%x) {dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3x2xf32>) -> tensor<3x2xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.reverse"(%x) {dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T) -> T`.

### stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim
broadcast_in_dim is written `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<2x3xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. Operand dimension d must either have size 1 or have the same size as result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d].         """

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types. 
### stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim
broadcast_in_dim is written `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<2x3xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. The result has the same element type as the operand. broadcast_dimensions must contain exactly one entry for each dimension of the operand. Each entry of broadcast_dimensions is a distinct result dimension index between 0 and the result rank minus one. Operand dimension d must either have size 1 or have the same size as result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d]. Operand dimension d is placed at result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d] and the data is copied along every other result dimension, while an operand dimension of size 1 is repeated across its whole result dimension. 
### stablehlo.reshape
reshape is written `%r = stablehlo.reshape %x : (tensor<2x3xf32>) -> tensor<6xf32>`. In general form: `%r = stablehlo.reshape %x : (T_in) -> T_out`. The operand and the result must contain the same number of elements. reshape keeps elements in row-major (lexicographic) order and never reorders them, so changing the order of axes requires a transpose. 
### stablehlo.reduce
reduce is written with a body region, for example `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<f32>, %b: tensor<f32>): %s = "stablehlo.add"(%a, %b) : (tensor<f32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<f32> "stablehlo.return"(%s) : (tensor<f32>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<4x3xf32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<4xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<E>, %b: tensor<E>): ... "stablehlo.return"(%v) : (tensor<E>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in, tensor<E>) -> T_out`. The init value is a rank-0 tensor whose element type equals the input's, and the body takes two rank-0 tensors of that element type and returns one. The result shape is the input shape with the reduced dimensions removed, not kept as size-1 dimensions. The reduced dimensions must be distinct and each between 0 and the input rank minus one. The init value may be combined an implementation-defined number of times, so it must be the identity of the body: zero for add, negative infinity for maximum and positive infinity for minimum. reduce can reduce several inputs at once: with N inputs and N init values the body takes 2N rank-0 arguments (the N accumulators, then the N elements) and returns N values, which is how an argmax carries a value together with its index. 
### stablehlo.compare
compare is written `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction LT>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type FLOAT>} : (tensor<4xf32>, tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xi1>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction DIR>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type CT>} : (T, T) -> tensor<...xi1>`. lhs and rhs have the same element type and the result element type is i1. compare_type is optional, but if given it must be FLOAT, TOTALORDER or WEAKORDER for floating-point operands and NOTYPE or SIGNED for signed integers. lhs, rhs and the result must have the same shape. ### stablehlo.select
select is written `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %on_true, %on_false) : (tensor<2x2xi1>, tensor<2x2xf32>, tensor<2x2xf32>) -> tensor<2x2xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %t, %f) : (tensor<...xi1>, T, T) -> T`. on_true, on_false and the result must have the same type. The predicate has element type i1 and is either rank 0 or the same shape as on_true. Each result element is taken from on_true where the predicate is true and from on_false otherwise. 
### stablehlo.convert
convert is written `%r = stablehlo.convert %x : (tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xi32>`. In general form: `%r = stablehlo.convert %x : (T_in) -> T_out`. The result has the same shape as the operand; only the element type changes. Float-to-integer conversion truncates the fractional part toward zero, a boolean converts to 0 or 1, and a number converts to a boolean as true exactly when it is non-zero. 
### stablehlo.dynamic_slice
dynamic_slice takes the operand followed by one rank-0 integer start index per dimension: `%r = "stablehlo.dynamic_slice"(%x, %i, %j) {slice_sizes = array<i64: 2, 4>} : (tensor<8x4xf32>, tensor<i32>, tensor<i32>) -> tensor<2x4xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.dynamic_slice"(%x, %s0, ..., %s_{R-1}) {slice_sizes = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in, tensor<I>, ...) -> T_out`. All start indices are rank-0 tensors of the same integer type, and the result element type equals the operand's. There is one start index and one slice size per operand dimension, each slice size is at most the dimension size, and the result shape equals slice_sizes. Before slicing, each start index is clamped into the range 0 to dimension size minus slice size, so an out-of-range start never fails but shifts the window inside the tensor.

Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types. 
### stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim
broadcast_in_dim is written `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<2x3xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. The result has the same element type as the operand. broadcast_dimensions must contain exactly one entry for each dimension of the operand. Each entry of broadcast_dimensions is a distinct result dimension index between 0 and the result rank minus one. Operand dimension d must either have size 1 or have the same size as result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d]. Operand dimension d is placed at result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d] and the data is copied along every other result dimension, while an operand dimension of size 1 is repeated across its whole result dimension. 
### stablehlo.reshape
reshape is written `%r = stablehlo.reshape %x : (tensor<2x3xf32>) -> tensor<6xf32>`. In general form: `%r = stablehlo.reshape %x : (T_in) -> T_out`. The operand and the result must contain the same number of elements. reshape keeps elements in row-major (lexicographic) order and never reorders them, so changing the order of axes requires a transpose. 
### stablehlo.transpose
transpose is written `%r = "stablehlo.transpose"(%x) {permutation = array<i64: 1, 0>} : (tensor<2x3xf32>) -> tensor<3x2xf32>`. Result dimension d has the size of operand dimension permutation[d]. ### stablehlo.dot_general
dot_general is written `%r = "stablehlo.dot_general"(%a, %b) {dot_dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.dot<lhs_batching_dimensions = [0], rhs_batching_dimensions = [0], lhs_contracting_dimensions = [2], rhs_contracting_dimensions = [1]>} : (tensor<2x3x4xf32>, tensor<2x4x5xf32>) -> tensor<2x3x5xf32>`, and the batching fields may be omitted when there are no batch dimensions. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<E>, %b: tensor<E>): ... "stablehlo.return"(%v) : (tensor<E>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in, tensor<E>) -> T_out`. The init value is a rank-0 tensor whose element type equals the input's, and the body takes two rank-0 tensors of that element type and returns one. The result shape is the input shape with the reduced dimensions removed, not kept as size-1 dimensions. The reduced dimensions must be distinct and each between 0 and the input rank minus one. The init value may be combined an implementation-defined number of times, so it must be the identity of the body: zero for add, negative infinity for maximum and positive infinity for minimum. reduce can reduce several inputs at once: with N inputs and N init values the body takes 2N rank-0 arguments (the N accumulators, then the N elements) and returns N values, which is how an argmax carries a value together with its index. 
### stablehlo.compare
compare is written `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction LT>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type FLOAT>} : (tensor<4xf32>, tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xi1>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction DIR>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type CT>} : (T, T) -> tensor<...xi1>`. lhs and rhs have the same element type and the result element type is i1. compare_type is optional, but if given it must be FLOAT, TOTALORDER or WEAKORDER for floating-point operands and NOTYPE or SIGNED for signed integers. lhs, rhs and the result must have the same shape. The direction EQ, NE, GE, GT, LE or LT tests lhs against rhs element-wise, for example GT gives true where lhs > rhs. 
### stablehlo.select
select is written `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %on_true, %on_false) : (tensor<2x2xi1>, tensor<2x2xf32>, tensor<2x2xf32>) -> tensor<2x2xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %t, %f) : (tensor<...xi1>, T, T) -> T`. on_true, on_false and the result must have the same type. The predicate has element type i1 and is either rank 0 or the same shape as on_true. Each result element is taken from on_true where the predicate is true and from on_false otherwise. 
### stablehlo.convert
convert is written `%r = stablehlo.convert %x : (tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xi32>`. In general form: `%r = stablehlo.convert %x : (T_in) -> T_out`. The result has the same shape as the operand; only the element type changes. Float-to-integer conversion truncates the fractional part toward zero, a boolean converts to 0 or 1, and a number converts to a boolean as true exactly when it is non-zero. 
### stablehlo.dynamic_slice
dynamic_slice takes the operand followed by one rank-0 integer start index per dimension: `%r = "stablehlo.dynamic_slice"(%x, %i, %j) {slice_sizes = array<i64: 2, 4>} : (tensor<8x4xf32>, tensor<i32>, tensor<i32>) -> tensor<2x4xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.dynamic_slice"(%x, %s0, ..., %s_{R-1}) {slice_sizes = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in, tensor<I>, ...) -> T_out`. There is one start index and one slice size per operand dimension, each slice size is at most the dimension size, and the result shape equals slice_sizes. ### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. ### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.compare
compare is written `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction LT>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type FLOAT>} : (tensor<4xf32>, tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xi1>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction DIR>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type CT>} : (T, T) -> tensor<...xi1>`. lhs and rhs have the same element type and the result element type is i1. compare_type is optional, but if given it must be FLOAT, TOTALORDER or WEAKORDER for floating-point operands and NOTYPE or SIGNED for signed integers. lhs, rhs and the result must have the same shape. The direction EQ, NE, GE, GT, LE or LT tests lhs against rhs element-wise, for example GT gives true where lhs > rhs. 
### stablehlo.select
select is written `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %on_true, %on_false) : (tensor<2x2xi1>, tensor<2x2xf32>, tensor<2x2xf32>) -> tensor<2x2xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %t, %f) : (tensor<...xi1>, T, T) -> T`. on_true, on_false and the result must have the same type. The predicate has element type i1 and is either rank 0 or the same shape as on_true. Each result element is taken from on_true where the predicate is true and from on_false otherwise. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`.

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.iota
iota is written `%r = "stablehlo.iota"() {iota_dimension = 0 : i64} : () -> tensor<4x5xi32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.iota"() {iota_dimension = d : i64} : () -> T`. iota_dimension must be between 0 and the result rank minus one. Each output element equals its own index along iota_dimension, so values count 0, 1, 2, ... along that dimension and are constant along every other dimension; float element types are allowed. 
### stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim
broadcast_in_dim is written `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<2x3xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. The result has the same element type as the operand. broadcast_dimensions must contain exactly one entry for each dimension of the operand. Each entry of broadcast_dimensions is a distinct result dimension index between 0 and the result rank minus one. Operand dimension d must either have size 1 or have the same size as result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d]. Operand dimension d is placed at result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d] and the data is copied along every other result dimension, while an operand dimension of size 1 is repeated across its whole result dimension. 
### stablehlo.compare
compare is written `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction LT>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type FLOAT>} : (tensor<4xf32>, tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xi1>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction DIR>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type CT>} : (T, T) -> tensor<...xi1>`. lhs and rhs have the same element type and the result element type is i1. compare_type is optional, but if given it must be FLOAT, TOTALORDER or WEAKORDER for floating-point operands and NOTYPE or SIGNED for signed integers. lhs, rhs and the result must have the same shape. The direction EQ, NE, GE, GT, LE or LT tests lhs against rhs element-wise, for example GT gives true where lhs > rhs. 
### stablehlo.select
select is written `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %on_true, %on_false) : (tensor<2x2xi1>, tensor<2x2xf32>, tensor<2x2xf32>) -> tensor<2x2xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %t, %f) : (tensor<...xi1>, T, T) -> T`. on_true, on_false and the result must have the same type. The predicate has element type i1 and is either rank 0 or the same shape as on_true. Each result element is taken from on_true where the predicate is true and from on_false otherwise. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`.

    """

    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, bias_shape):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.conv_transpose = nn.ConvTranspose2d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size)

        x = torch.mean(x, dim=(2, 3), keepdim=True)  # Global average pooling

        x = torch.sum(x, dim=(2, 3))  # Sum
        x = x * 10.0  # Multiplication

### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types. 
### stablehlo.math
Further element-wise math operations are written like `%r = stablehlo.tanh %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise log, log_plus_one, exponential_minus_one, logistic, floor, sign) and `%r = stablehlo.power %a, %b : tensor<4xf32>`. In general form: unary := `%r = stablehlo.{tanh|log|log_plus_one|exponential_minus_one|logistic|floor|sign} %a : T`; binary := `%r = stablehlo.power %a, %b : T`. logistic computes 1 / (1 + exp(-x)), log_plus_one computes log(1 + x), exponential_minus_one computes exp(x) - 1, and power raises each lhs element to the corresponding rhs element, so both operands must already have the same shape. 
### stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim
broadcast_in_dim is written `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<2x3xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. The result has the same element type as the operand. broadcast_dimensions must contain exactly one entry for each dimension of the operand. Each entry of broadcast_dimensions is a distinct result dimension index between 0 and the result rank minus one. Operand dimension d must either have size 1 or have the same size as result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d]. Operand dimension d is placed at result dimension broadcast_dimensions[d] and the data is copied along every other result dimension, while an operand dimension of size 1 is repeated across its whole result dimension. 
### stablehlo.reshape
reshape is written `%r = stablehlo.reshape %x : (tensor<2x3xf32>) -> tensor<6xf32>`. In general form: `%r = stablehlo.reshape %x : (T_in) -> T_out`. The operand and the result must contain the same number of elements. reshape keeps elements in row-major (lexicographic) order and never reorders them, so changing the order of axes requires a transpose. 
### stablehlo.convolution
convolution is written `%r = "stablehlo.convolution"(%x, %w) {window_strides = array<i64: 1, 1>, padding = dense<[[1, 1], [1, 1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>, lhs_dilation = array<i64: 1, 1>, rhs_dilation = array<i64: 1, 1>, dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.conv<[b, f, 0, 1]x[o, i, 0, 1]->[b, f, 0, 1]>, feature_group_count = 1 : i64, batch_group_count = 1 : i64} : (tensor<2x3x8x8xf32>, tensor<4x3x3x3xf32>) -> tensor<2x4x8x8xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.convolution"(%lhs, %rhs) {window_strides = array<i64: ...>, padding = dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<(N-2)x2xi64>, lhs_dilation = array<i64: ...>, rhs_dilation = array<i64: ...>, dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.conv<[...]x[...]->[...]>, feature_group_count = G : i64, batch_group_count = 1 : i64} : (T_lhs, T_rhs) -> T_out`. The input, kernel and result have the same element type. dimension_numbers lists the role of each dimension: in the input and output b is batch, f is feature and 0, 1, ... are spatial dimensions; in the kernel o is output feature, i is input feature and 0, 1, ... are spatial; for example `[b, f, 0, 1]x[o, i, 0, 1]->[b, f, 0, 1]` is the NCHW / OIHW layout. window_strides, lhs_dilation and rhs_dilation each have one positive entry per spatial dimension, and padding has one [low, high] pair per spatial dimension. Each output spatial size is floor((low + (n - 1) * lhs_dilation + 1 + high - ((k - 1) * rhs_dilation + 1)) / stride) + 1, where n is the input size and k the kernel size along that dimension. The kernel's input-feature size equals the input feature size divided by feature_group_count, and the kernel's output-feature size, which becomes the output feature size, must be divisible by feature_group_count. convolution computes a cross-correlation without flipping the kernel; rhs_dilation spaces out kernel taps (dilated convolution), lhs_dilation inserts lhs_dilation - 1 zeros between input elements (used for transposed convolution together with a spatially reversed kernel), and feature_group_count splits the features into independent groups (grouped or depthwise convolution). 
### stablehlo.reduce
reduce is written with a body region, for example `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<f32>, %b: tensor<f32>): %s = "stablehlo.add"(%a, %b) : (tensor<f32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<f32> "stablehlo.return"(%s) : (tensor<f32>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<4x3xf32>, tensor<f32>) -> tensor<4xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<E>, %b: tensor<E>): ... "stablehlo.return"(%v) : (tensor<E>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in, tensor<E>) -> T_out`. The init value is a rank-0 tensor whose element type equals the input's, and the body takes two rank-0 tensors of that element type and returns one. The result shape is the input shape with the reduced dimensions removed, not kept as size-1 dimensions. The reduced dimensions must be distinct and each between 0 and the input rank minus one. The init value may be combined an implementation-defined number of times, so it must be the identity of the body: zero for add, negative infinity for maximum and positive infinity for minimum. reduce can reduce several inputs at once: with N inputs and N init values the body takes 2N rank-0 arguments (the N accumulators, then the N elements) and returns N values, which is how an argmax carries a value together with its index. 
### stablehlo.compare
compare is written `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction LT>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type FLOAT>} : (tensor<4xf32>, tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xi1>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.compare"(%a, %b) {comparison_direction = #stablehlo<comparison_direction DIR>, compare_type = #stablehlo<comparison_type CT>} : (T, T) -> tensor<...xi1>`. lhs and rhs have the same element type and the result element type is i1. compare_type is optional, but if given it must be FLOAT, TOTALORDER or WEAKORDER for floating-point operands and NOTYPE or SIGNED for signed integers. lhs, rhs and the result must have the same shape. The direction EQ, NE, GE, GT, LE or LT tests lhs against rhs element-wise, for example GT gives true where lhs > rhs. 
### stablehlo.select
select is written `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %on_true, %on_false) : (tensor<2x2xi1>, tensor<2x2xf32>, tensor<2x2xf32>) -> tensor<2x2xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.select"(%pred, %t, %f) : (tensor<...xi1>, T, T) -> T`. on_true, on_false and the result must have the same type. The predicate has element type i1 and is either rank 0 or the same shape as on_true. Each result element is taken from on_true where the predicate is true and from on_false otherwise. 
### stablehlo.reverse
reverse is written `%r = "stablehlo.reverse"(%x) {dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3x2xf32>) -> tensor<3x2xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.reverse"(%x) {dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T) -> T`. The result has the operand's type, and dimensions are distinct indices between 0 and the rank minus one. class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Simple model that performs a 3D convolution, applies minimum operation along a specific dimension, 
    and then applies softmax.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, dim):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.conv = nn.Conv3d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size)
        self.dim = dim

        x = torch.min(x, dim=self.dim)[0]  # Apply minimum along the specified dimension
        x = torch.softmax(x, dim=1)  # Apply softmax along the channel dimension
        return x

    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size, dim):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.conv = nn.Conv3d(in_channels, out_channels, kernel_size)

In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. A tensor type is written with its dimension sizes and element type, such as `tensor<4x3xf32>`, and a scalar is a rank-0 tensor such as `tensor<f32>`; the element types used here are f32, i32, i64 and i1 (boolean). StableHLO performs no implicit broadcasting, rank promotion or type promotion, so every operand must already have exactly the shape and element type that the operation requires. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. The literal's type must equal the result type, and a single-value literal such as `dense<0.0> : tensor<4x3xf32>` fills every element of the tensor. Floating-point infinities are written as hexadecimal bit patterns: negative infinity in f32 is `dense<0xFF800000>` and positive infinity is `dense<0x7F800000>`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have the same element type. All operands and the result of an element-wise operation must have identical shapes, so a vector or scalar is never combined with a matrix without an explicit broadcast_in_dim first. Integer divide rounds toward zero, and exponential, sqrt and rsqrt are defined only for floating-point element types. 
### stablehlo.math
Further element-wise math operations are written like `%r = stablehlo.tanh %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise log, log_plus_one, exponential_minus_one, logistic, floor, sign) and `%r = stablehlo.power %a, %b : tensor<4xf32>`. ### stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim
broadcast_in_dim is written `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<2x3xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`. ### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. In general form: program := `func.func @main(%arg: T, ...) -> T_out { op* ; return %v : T_out }`; each %name defined once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`. In general form: int_list_attr := `array<i64: d0, d1, ...>` (NOT `dense<[...]> : tensor<Nxi64>`); int_attr := `N : i64`; padding (convolution, reduce_window) := `dense<[[lo, hi], ...]> : tensor<Rx2xi64>`. 
### stablehlo.constant
A constant is written `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<0.0> : tensor<f32>` or in generic form `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<[1.0, 2.0]> : tensor<2xf32>} : () -> tensor<2xf32>`. In general form: `%c = stablehlo.constant dense<v> : T` | `%c = "stablehlo.constant"() {value = dense<...> : T} : () -> T`. 
### Element-wise operations
Binary element-wise operations are written `%r = stablehlo.add %a, %b : tensor<4x3xf32>` (likewise subtract, multiply, divide, maximum, minimum) and unary ones are written `%r = stablehlo.exponential %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise negate, sqrt, rsqrt, abs). In general form: binary := `%r = stablehlo.{add|subtract|multiply|divide|maximum|minimum} %a, %b : T`; unary := `%r = stablehlo.{exponential|negate|sqrt|rsqrt|abs} %a : T`. 
### stablehlo.math
Further element-wise math operations are written like `%r = stablehlo.tanh %a : tensor<4xf32>` (likewise log, log_plus_one, exponential_minus_one, logistic, floor, sign) and `%r = stablehlo.power %a, %b : tensor<4xf32>`. In general form: unary := `%r = stablehlo.{tanh|log|log_plus_one|exponential_minus_one|logistic|floor|sign} %a : T`; binary := `%r = stablehlo.power %a, %b : T`. 
### stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim
broadcast_in_dim is written `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: 1>} : (tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<2x3xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.broadcast_in_dim"(%x) {broadcast_dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in) -> T_out`.

reshape is written `%r = stablehlo.reshape %x : (tensor<2x3xf32>) -> tensor<6xf32>`. In general form: `%r = stablehlo.reshape %x : (T_in) -> T_out`.

convolution is written `%r = "stablehlo.convolution"(%x, %w) {window_strides = array<i64: 1, 1>, padding = dense<[[1, 1], [1, 1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>, lhs_dilation = array<i64: 1, 1>, rhs_dilation = array<i64: 1, 1>, dimension_numbers = #stablehlo.conv<[b, f, 0, 1]x[o, i, 0, 1]->[b, f, 0, 1]>, feature_group_count = 1 : i64, batch_group_count = 1 : i64} : (tensor<2x3x8x8xf32>, tensor<4x3x3x3xf32>) -> tensor<2x4x8x8xf32>`. In general form: `%r = "stablehlo.reduce"(%x, %init) ({ ^bb0(%a: tensor<E>, %b: tensor<E>): ... "stablehlo.return"(%v) : (tensor<E>) -> () }) {dimensions = array<i64: ...>} : (T_in, tensor<E>) -> T_out`. The init value is a rank-0 tensor whose element type equals the input's, and the body takes two rank-0 tensors of that element type and returns one. import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Model(nn.Module):
    """
    Simple model that performs a matrix multiplication, scales the result, and applies batch normalization.
    """
    def __init__(self, in_features, out_features, scale_shape, eps=1e-5, momentum=0.1):
        super(Model, self).__init__()
        self.gemm = nn.Linear(in_features, out_features)
        self.scale = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(scale_shape))
        self.bn = nn.BatchNorm1d(out_features, eps=eps, momentum=momentum)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.gemm(x)
        x = x * self.scale
        x = self.bn(x)
        return x

    return [torch.rand(batch_size, in_features)]

    return [in_features, out_features, scale_shape]

A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. ### Program structure and types
A program is a single MLIR function named @main, written as `func.func @main(%x: tensor<4x3xf32>, %b: tensor<3xf32>) -> tensor<4x3xf32> { ... return %r : tensor<4x3xf32> }`, and every value is an SSA name that is defined exactly once. Any operation can be written in generic form as `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(%a, %b) {attr = value} : (type_of_a, type_of_b) -> type_of_r`, where the trailing function type lists every operand type and the result type exactly. In general form: op := `%r = "stablehlo.NAME"(operands) {attrs}? : (operand_types) -> result_type`. One-dimensional integer-list attributes (dimensions, permutation, strides, slice and padding lists) are written like `array<i64: 0, 1>`, never in the older `dense<[0, 1]> : tensor<2xi64>` form; a single integer attribute is written like `1 : i64`; the only two-dimensional attribute used here is the `padding` of convolution and reduce_window, written `dense<[[lo0, hi0], [lo1, hi1]]> : tensor<2x2xi64>`.
